title: Audience component library
rule: EVERY audience surface builds from these `<aha-*>` elements by default: a slide that hand-rolls a tappable answer row, a submit button or a waiting screen instead is a defect, even when it looks right. They are framework-free custom elements, so a build-less Developer Platform slide (a cross-origin iframe) loads them by URL: one version-pinned `lib/audience.js` (just the audience set, also exports `applyDeck`) plus `tokens.css`, then `applyDeck(document.documentElement, xprops.slide)` from `audience-deck.js` so every element takes the deck's ink, accent and font. The qualifier is PURPOSE, not taste: a slide with no answer options does not import the answer list; a slide that needs a tappable row does not hand-roll one.
why: The library is where six guarantees are implemented once: deck-tracking ink (from `slide.textColour`), the frosted surface that survives a photographic deck, the 44px touch floor, the submission lock that survives an iframe remount (`lock-key`), host-delegated image upload (`xprops.uploadImage`), and the deck font on every `<button>` (`font: inherit`). A hand-rolled control re-opens all six, and every one of them has already cost review rounds. Each section names the element to use; the upstream Vue name (`@/iframe/audience`) stays as the heading so a port can find its match.

sections.name: AnswerOptionList
sections.what: The whole answer block: rows, single or multiple selection, the 8px thumb-safety gap (fixed, no prop), optional live counts, and the quiz reveal.
sections.useWhen: A MULTIPLE-CHOICE question: a fixed set of predefined answers the participant picks from, one of them, or several with `selection-mode="multiple"`. This is the default answer surface and covers nearly every quiz and poll; pass `options`, a `lock-key` and the host quiz flags, and it carries the rest.
sections.notFor: Anything the participant composes or positions rather than picks: free text, a scale (`<aha-scale-slider>`), a drawing, an image. Also not a set of filters or tags toggled without submitting: short inline toggles are `<aha-audience-chip>`.
sections.replaces: Replaces a hand-built tappable answer row — a tappable row carries the submission lock, the deck ink, the frosted surface and the deck accent — hand-rolling the row re-opens all four

sections.name: AnswerOption
sections.what: One tappable answer row, driven entirely by a state object rather than by working its own state out.
sections.useWhen: The rare answer screen that is NOT a plain list: rows split across columns, interleaved with other content, or laid out on a board. Set the raw quiz flags as attributes; the row resolves them with `answerOptionState()`.
sections.notFor: An ordinary list of options. `<aha-answer-list>` already repeats this row and owns the gap, the selection mode and the counts.
sections.note: Shown answered and revealed, the state with the most moving parts: a tick or cross on every row, the correct row ringed in the success colour, the participant's own wrong pick ringed and tinted in the error colour, and the other rows muted.

sections.name: DraggableOptions
sections.what: A reorderable list: "put the options in the correct order". Each row wears the answer row's frosted surface and ink edge plus a live ordinal badge; the participant reorders by dragging a row or with its up and down buttons. `value` is the ordered id array. An option's image is shown IN FULL (contain, never cropped).
sections.useWhen: The answer IS an ordering — ranking, sequencing, "sort these". The model you submit is the order itself, not a pick.
sections.notFor: Choosing option(s) from a set: that is `<aha-answer-list>` (single or multiple). Ordering is a different answer shape.
sections.note: Drag a row, or reorder from the keyboard with the up and down buttons: the badges renumber live and every move is announced. `value` is the ordered id array.

sections.name: Input
sections.what: A single-line text field: the shared DS `<aha-counted-input size="touch">` (56px, a FIXED white fill and dark ink that do not track the deck) inside `<aha-audience-field>`, whose label above DOES track the deck ink and becomes the field's accessible name.
sections.useWhen: The participant types one short line: a name, a word, a short answer. The label reads on a light deck and a dark one; the field stays white either way.
sections.notFor: A number (`type="number"`, below), a long free-text answer (the textarea), or a pick from a fixed set (`<aha-select>` / `<aha-answer-list>`).
sections.replaces: Replaces a hand-built `<input>`: the DS field already carries the 56px sizing, the resting, hover and focus borders and the counter; a hand-rolled one re-opens the height, the label and the contrast.
sections.note: The counter shows on focus; `maxlength="none"` drops the cap.

sections.name: InputNumber
sections.what: A numeric field: `<aha-counted-input type="number" maxlength="none" size="touch">` (a numeric keypad on a phone, 56px, fixed white fill and dark ink) inside `<aha-audience-field>`.
sections.useWhen: The participant enters a NUMBER: a quantity, a count, a score, an age.
sections.notFor: Free text or a pick from a fixed set. A number on a small range the participant nudges rather than types is `<aha-scale-slider>`.
sections.replaces: Replaces a hand-built `<input type="number">` and the upstream stepper field: the browser's own number keypad replaces the steppers on a phone, and the 56px DS field keeps the touch floor (the 40px `<aha-input size="lg">` does not).
sections.note: The value is the field's text; parse it with `Number()` and treat an empty string as no answer.

sections.name: Select
sections.what: A dropdown: the shared DS `<aha-select size="touch">` (fixed white trigger, dark ink) inside `<aha-audience-field>`, whose label tracks the deck ink.
sections.useWhen: The participant picks ONE value from a longer or space-constrained list where showing every option as a row would be too much: a country, a category.
sections.notFor: A short set of predefined answers to a question: that is `<aha-answer-list>`, which carries the 44px rows and the reveal states. Chips beat a dropdown when every choice fits on screen.
sections.replaces: Replaces a hand-built `<select>`: the DS select carries the sizing, borders, keyboard and listbox roles.
sections.note: Options come from the `options` attribute or property; a disabled option is shown greyed.

sections.name: Timer
sections.what: A countdown: a bar that drains as the time runs out, with the m:ss clock beside it. One CSS animation off an absolute `ends-at`, never a per-frame loop.
sections.useWhen: A FULL-CANVAS audience slide whose question is time-limited and needs its own timer. Pass the host's absolute end instant, not a duration.
sections.notFor: A framed slide: the host already paints the countdown above the iframe. Use `clock-only` for a bare m:ss in a tight header. Not a progress bar for anything that is not time.
sections.replaces: Replaces a hand-built countdown: a per-tick counter drifts on a backgrounded tab and runs the compositor for the whole question.

sections.name: ScaleSlider
sections.what: A rating scale: a native range input themed to the deck, with a label at each end and a live readout of the value and its step label.
sections.useWhen: The participant rates one statement on a range. Set `accent` from the deck palette by the statement's position, so each row keeps the colour the canvas gives it.
sections.notFor: A two-ended range selection, or a slider that sets a quantity in a settings panel: that is `<aha-slider>`.
sections.replaces: Replaces a raw `input[type=range]`: the element keeps the native keyboard and slider role and adds the deck theme, the unset state and commit-on-drag.

sections.name: SubmitButton
sections.what: The ONE primary submit action per audience screen: `<aha-button variant="primary" size="touch" block>` wrapped with the audience contract. Fill = the deck accent (`applyDeck` sets `--aha-button-primary-*`) with a readable black or white label; disabled = the DS grey; the deck font inherited into the button; busy on tap; then `lock(value)` writes the submission lock under `lock-key`, which survives an iframe remount, or `unlock()` lets the participant retry.
sections.useWhen: The screen has a submit, lock-in or place-bid action. Listen for `submit-answer`, call the host, then `lock(answer)` or `unlock()`. Add `closed` when the host stops submissions.
sections.notFor: A secondary or tertiary action (skip, change, back) or a destructive remove: those use `<aha-button>` secondary or tertiary. Two primaries on one screen means neither is the submit.
sections.note: Tap it: busy, then locked. The lock caption and the closed caption replace the label in place, so nothing reflows.

<!-- Paste-and-run: save as .html and open it. No build step, nothing to copy.
     In a Developer Platform slide type, applyDeck() gives every audience element the deck's ink, accent
     and font from the host's slide props (the host's --aha-* variables never reach the iframe). -->

<!-- <script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ahaslides-product/ahaslides-design@__REF__/lib/audience.js"></script> -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ahaslides-product/ahaslides-design@__REF__/lib/tokens.css">
<script type="module">
  import 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ahaslides-product/ahaslides-design@__REF__/lib/aha-audience-submit.js';
  import 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ahaslides-product/ahaslides-design@__REF__/lib/aha-answer-list.js';   // registers <aha-audience-submit>
  import { applyDeck } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ahaslides-product/ahaslides-design@__REF__/lib/audience-deck.js';
  applyDeck(document.documentElement, window.xprops?.slide ?? { textColour: '#1A1A1A', presentationColorPalette: ['#E70E68'] });
  const submit = document.querySelector('aha-audience-submit');
  submit.addEventListener('submit-answer', async () => {
    const answer = document.querySelector('aha-answer-list').value;
    try {
      await window.xprops?.submit?.(answer);   // the host call in a real slide
      submit.lock(answer);                     // locks every element sharing lock-key, across remounts
    } catch {
      submit.unlock();                         // let the participant try again
    }
  });
</script>

sections.name: Card
sections.what: A swipeable content card on the deck's own surface — the frosted wash plus an ink hairline, with the deliberate-travel threshold and the spring-back already in it.
sections.useWhen: The SWIPE-CARD shape: the participant is handed one thing at a time and throws it left or right to answer (this-or-that, would-you-rather, a sorting deck). That is what this is for, and the gesture is on by default because of it.
sections.notFor: A static panel. `static` exists for the odd card in a swipe deck that must not move, not as a way to get a generic box: for the frosted surface alone, use `audienceSurface()` / `audienceBorder()` from `audience-deck.js` on your own element. Never wrap the whole audience screen: the screen is transparent over the deck by contract.
sections.replaces: Replaces a generic card or a bespoke panel: an opaque card surface reads as a foreign block on a dark deck.
sections.note: Drag it sideways, or focus it and press an arrow key: past 72px or on a flick it commits, below that it springs back.

sections.name: Helpers
sections.what: Plain functions, no element. `applyDeck(root, slide)` turns the host's slide props into the deck variables every audience element reads; `submissionLock(key)` is the lock behind `lock-key`; `audienceSurface()` / `audienceBorder()` give the frosted surface and hairline for your own element; `answerOptionState()` interprets the quiz lifecycle for one row.
sections.useWhen: Call `applyDeck` once when the slide props arrive (and again when they change). Reach for `answerOptionState` whenever you render `<aha-answer-option>` yourself, so a slide never has to know what quizStatus 4 means.
sections.notFor: Styling a DS element from outside: set `ink` / `accent` on it, or call `applyDeck`, instead of overriding its private variables.

// -> { visible, interactive, dimmed, tone, verdict, mine }
const lock = submissionLock(`slide-${slide.id}`);   // survives an iframe remount (sessionStorage)
